Incident Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: High error rate and elevated tail latency observed in northamerica-east1 (zone east1b). Affected service: inference-runtime (model shards 1-3). Error rate: 5xx spike ~18% since 00:32 UTC. Paging on-call. Please acknowledge and triage. Metrics: grafana.redwood.com/d/serve/latency?orgId=1

Aj K: acked. I'm oncall and looking now. grabbing logs from the gateway + edge pools. pinging @Dinesh P to check infra layer. I'll take first 15m. :eyes:

Dinesh P: looking at egress/zn-east1b hostpool logs — seeing connection resets and kube-proxy restarts on 3 nodes around 00:30. backend 502/503. suspecting a faulty kernel update rolled during the maintenance window. pulling nodepool logs.

Maya R: before any destructive action, recommend diverting new traffic for shards 1-3 away from east1b to northamerica-west2 and us-central1 via SmartRouter policy so we don't impact customer requests while we restart nodes. I can flip the route in SmartRouter (non-disruptive). :+1:

Aj K: agree. Maya, please perform diversion, and post the SmartRouter command you used here so we can revert later. I'll prepare restart playbooks for the affected nodes.

Maya R: running diversion now. command:```bash
curl -X POST https://smartrouter.internal.api/v1/policy/divert \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from":"northamerica-east1","to":["northamerica-west2","us-central1"],"weight":100,"shards":[1,2,3],"reason":"emergency-diversion-east1b-2026-03-15"}'
```
response: {"status":"accepted","change_id":"sr-9a2f"}. New requests should start shifting within ~30s. Posting to #eng-runtime when shift observed.

Incident Bot: DRAFT status page update (please review):
"We are currently investigating increased error rates and high latency for inference requests originating in northamerica-east1. We have initiated traffic diversion to alternate regions and are performing node restarts in the affected zone. Impact: partial request errors and increased latency for some customers in NA east. Status: Mitigating. Next update in 15 minutes."

Sara W: I can take the customer-facing note. Short draft for support/status page email: 
"We are investigating an issue affecting inference requests in the North America (east) region. Some requests may return errors or experience higher latency. Our engineers have diverted traffic to alternate regions and are working on node restarts. We will provide updates every 15 minutes. No action required from customers. — Redwood Inference Status Team"

Support Bot: queued draft to support queue for pre-approval. tagging @Product Ops for severity classification and whether we escalate to customers via status.redwood.com/publisher.

Product Ops: Severity: P2 (partial degradation, customer-facing errors). Recommend publishing initial status page message and sending to customers who have SLA alerts configured. Approving support note.

Dinesh P: performing rolling restart of nodepool-east1b-neo. command:```bash
gcloud compute instances reset nodepool-east1b-0 --zone=east1b
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy --field-selector metadata.name=nodepool-east1b
```
Restarting node 0/3 -> 1/3 -> 2/3. Monitoring. Initial results: error rate drops to ~7% after first node comes up.

Aj K: monitoring traces. KV cache miss rate still higher than baseline 00:00, which explains residual latency. Dinesh, any chance the kernel update removed an iptables conntrack tuning?

Dinesh P: yes, conntrack_max looks reduced. I've applied temporary sysctl to bump conntrack and kicked cache warmers. command:```bash
ssh node-1
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
kubectl -n cache rollout restart deployment/cache-warmer
```
After sysctl, latency 95th improves back to baseline in ~4 minutes.

Aj K: good. I'm going to capture final logs and prepare incident timeline. Will hand off to @Maya R for monitoring + follow-up. Handing over at 00:55 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Maya R: taking over. I'll keep the diversion in place for 45 minutes to ensure steady traffic. Posting the status page update now. Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.com/incident/2026-03-15-northamerica-east1

Sara W: customer email sent to affected customers list (customers.na-east). copy of sent message: "We diverted traffic and are performing remediation; you may see reduced errors now. We'll update again in 30 minutes."

Incident Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation in progress. Diversion active, nodepool restarts completed, sysctl applied, cache warmers restarted. Error rate down to <1% and latency returning to normal. Monitoring for 30m.

Product Ops: marking incident status as "Mitigated (monitoring)" on internal tracker. Deciding on post-incident review and whether to roll back emergency SmartRouter rule or keep as precaution.

Aj K: quick postmortem notes for later: cause = kernel update + reduced conntrack tuning during maintenance; impact = partial errors and latency for NA-east; mitigation = traffic diversion via SmartRouter, node restarts, sysctl bump, cache warmers. Action items: 1) pin kernel images for rolling updates, 2) add conntrack validation to node healthcheck, 3) automate SmartRouter emergency revert play.

Maya R: I'll keep monitoring for the next hour. If everything looks stable, I'll revert diversion and remove the emergency rule, then post final update.

Incident Bot: Final planned update at 01:40 UTC. If no regression, incident will be closed then and a postmortem scheduled. :calendar:
